lesson.value: No rocket of its day could throw Juno straight to Jupiter. Juno launched on an Atlas V on Aug. 5, 2011, flew back past Earth 26 months later to pick up speed from Earth's gravity (a gravity assist), and reached Jupiter on July 4, 2016.
lesson.source: NASA Science: Juno (launch Aug. 5, 2011 on an Atlas V; returned past Earth 26 months later and sped away with greater energy; reached Jupiter July 4, 2016)
